source: Read from the tool definitions in the mintplexlabs/anythingllm:1.16 image (server/utils/agents/aibitat/plugins), 2026-09-24.

web-scraping.description: Read and extract content from a specific webpage URL. Fetch the text from a website, get the contents of a link, or visit a URL to see what it says. Use when you have a specific web address to read.

params.name: url
params.description: A complete web address URL including protocol. Assumes https if not provided.

web-browsing.description: Search the internet for real-time information. Look online for current news, recent updates, latest changes, or any information not available locally. Browse the web to find answers about current events, prices, weather, or live data.

params.name: query
params.description: A search query.

document-summarizer.description: List all documents in the workspace or summarize a specific document. See what files are available, get a summary of a document's contents, or read and condense a file into key points.

params.name: action
params.description: The action to take. 'list' will return all files available with their filename and descriptions. 'summarize' will open and summarize the file by the a document name.

params.name: document_filename
params.description: The file name of the document you want to get the full content of.

rag-memory.description: Search your local documents and workspace files for relevant information, or store information to long-term memory. Use search to find answers in uploaded documents, embedded files, or previously stored memories. Use store only when explicitly asked to remember or save something.

params.name: action
params.description: The action we want to take to search for existing similar context or storage of new context.

params.name: content
params.description: The plain text to search our local documents with or to store in our vector database.

create-chart.description: Create a chart, graph, or data visualization. Generate bar charts, line graphs, pie charts, area charts, or scatter plots to visualize data, statistics, trends, or results. Use to display numbers and data visually.

params.name: type
params.type: area | bar | line | composed | scatter | pie | radar | radialBar | treemap | funnel
params.description: The type of chart to be generated.

params.name: title
params.description: Title of the chart. There MUST always be a title. Do not leave it blank.

params.name: dataset
params.description:
Valid JSON in which each element is an object for Recharts API for the 'type' of chart defined WITHOUT new line characters. Strictly using this FORMAT and naming:
{ "name": "a", "value": 12 }].
Make sure field "name" always stays named "name". Instead of naming value field value in JSON, name it based on user metric and make it the same across every item.
Make sure the format use double quotes and property names are string literals. Provide JSON data only.

generate-image.description: Generate an image from a text prompt, or edit an image already in the conversation. Use for any request to draw, create, render, or modify a picture. Images the user attached and images generated earlier in the chat are sourced from the conversation automatically - never describe or re-encode them into the prompt.

params.name: prompt
params.description: Detailed description of the image to create, or of the change to apply when editing.

params.name: size
params.description: Image dimensions as WIDTHxHEIGHT (eg: 512x512, 1024x1024). Omit to use the system default.

params.name: edit
params.description: Set true to edit an image already in the conversation - one the user attached or one generated earlier - instead of creating a new one. The image itself is found automatically.

sql-list-databases.description: List all available databases via `list_databases` you currently have access to. Returns a unique string identifier `database_id` that can be used for future calls.

sql-list-tables.description: List all available tables in a database via its `database_id`.

params.name: database_id
params.description: The database identifier for which we will list all tables for. This is a required parameter

sql-get-table-schema.description: Gets the table schema in SQL for a given `table` and `database_id`

params.name: database_id
params.description: The database identifier for which we will connect to to query the table schema. This is a required field.

params.name: table_name
params.description: The database identifier for the table name we want the schema for. This is a required field.

sql-query.description: Run a read-only SQL query on a `database_id` which will return up rows of data related to the query. The query must only be SELECT statements which do not modify the table data. There should be a reasonable LIMIT on the return quantity to prevent long-running or queries which crash the db.

params.name: database_id
params.description: The database identifier for which we will connect to to query the table schema. This is required to run the SQL query.

params.name: sql_query
params.description: The raw SQL query to run. Should be a query which does not modify the table and will return results.

filesystem-read-text-file.description: Read the contents of a file from the file system. Supports many file types: text, code, PDFs, Word docs, audio/video (transcribed to text), and more. Image files (png, jpg, jpeg, gif, webp, svg, bmp) are automatically attached for you to view and analyze visually. IMPORTANT: Only use this tool when you know the exact file path. If you don't know where a file is located, use 'filesystem-search-files' first to find it (e.g., search for '*.csv' or the filename). Use the 'head' parameter to read only the first N lines, or 'tail' for the last N lines (text files only). Only works within allowed directories.

params.name: path
params.description: The path to the file to read. Can be relative to the allowed directory or absolute within allowed directories.

params.name: head
params.description: If provided, returns only the first N lines of the file.

params.name: tail
params.description: If provided, returns only the last N lines of the file.

filesystem-read-multiple-files.description: Read multiple files at once when you know their exact paths. Supports many file types: text, code, PDFs, Word docs, audio/video (transcribed to text), and more. Image files (png, jpg, jpeg, gif, webp, svg, bmp) are automatically attached for you to view and analyze visually. IMPORTANT: If you don't know the file paths, use 'filesystem-search-files' first with 'includeFileContents: true' to find and read files in one step. Each file's content is returned with its path. Failed reads won't stop the operation.

params.name: paths
params.description: Array of file paths to read. Each path must be a string pointing to a valid file within allowed directories.

filesystem-write-text-file.description: Create a new text file or completely overwrite an existing text file with new content. Use with caution as it will overwrite existing files without warning. Only handles text/plaintext content with proper encoding. Only works within allowed directories. For binary formats (PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX), use the appropriate document creation tools instead.

params.name: path
params.description: The path where the file should be created or overwritten.

params.name: content
params.description: The content to write to the file.

filesystem-edit-file.description: Make line-based edits to a text file. Each edit replaces exact line sequences with new content. Returns a git-style diff showing the changes made. Use dryRun=true to preview changes without applying them. Only works within allowed directories.

params.name: path
params.description: The path to the file to edit.

params.name: edits
params.description: Array of edit operations to apply.

params.name: dryRun
params.description: If true, preview changes using git-style diff format without applying them.

filesystem-create-directory.description: Create a new directory or ensure a directory exists. Can create multiple nested directories in one operation. If the directory already exists, this operation will succeed silently. Perfect for setting up directory structures for projects or ensuring required paths exist. Only works within allowed directories.

params.name: path
params.description: The path of the directory to create. Can include nested paths.

filesystem-list-directory.description: Get a detailed listing of all files and directories in a specified path. Results clearly distinguish between files and directories with [FILE] and [DIR] prefixes. Optionally includes file sizes and can sort by name or size. This tool is essential for understanding directory structure and finding specific files within a directory. Only works within allowed directories.

params.name: path
params.description: The path of the directory to list.

params.name: includeSizes
params.description: If true, include file sizes in the listing.

params.name: sortBy
params.description: Sort entries by name or size.

filesystem-move-file.description: Move or rename files and directories. Can move files between directories and rename them in a single operation. If the destination exists, the operation will fail. Works across different directories and can be used for simple renaming within the same directory. Both source and destination must be within allowed directories.

params.name: source
params.description: The path of the file or directory to move.

params.name: destination
params.description: The destination path where the file or directory should be moved to.

filesystem-copy-file.description: Copy files and directories. Creates a duplicate of the source at the destination path. For directories, performs a recursive copy of all contents. If the destination exists, the operation will fail. Both source and destination must be within allowed directories.

params.name: source
params.description: The path of the file or directory to copy.

params.name: destination
params.description: The destination path where the copy should be created.

filesystem-search-files.description: Search for files by name or content. USE THIS FIRST when you need to find a file but don't know its exact location. Two modes: 'glob' matches file paths/names (e.g., '*.csv', 'config'), 'content' searches inside files using regex (like grep). Set 'includeFileContents: true' to also read and return the full contents of matching files in a single operation (useful when you need to find AND read files). Simple patterns like 'sales.csv' automatically match files containing that string anywhere.

params.name: pattern
params.description: For glob mode: a glob pattern to match file paths. For content mode: the text or regex pattern to search for in file contents.

params.name: mode
params.description: Search mode: 'glob' for matching file paths, 'content' for searching file contents.

params.name: filePattern
params.description: For content mode only: glob pattern to filter which files to search (e.g., '*.js', '*.{ts,tsx}').

params.name: excludePatterns
params.description: Patterns to exclude from search (e.g., 'node_modules', '*.log').

params.name: caseSensitive
params.description: For content mode: whether the search should be case-sensitive.

params.name: maxResults
params.description: Maximum number of results to return.

params.name: includeFileContents
params.description: If true, read and return the full contents of matching files (limited by maxFilesToRead). Useful when you need to analyze files, not just find them.

params.name: maxFilesToRead
params.description: When includeFileContents is true, maximum number of files to read contents from.

filesystem-get-file-info.description: Retrieve detailed metadata about a file or directory. Returns comprehensive information including size, creation time, last modified time, permissions, and type. This tool is perfect for understanding file characteristics without reading the actual content. Only works within allowed directories.

params.name: path
params.description: The path to the file or directory to get information about.

create-pptx-presentation.description: Create a professional PowerPoint presentation (PPTX). Provide a title, theme, and section outlines with key points. Each section is independently researched and built by a focused sub-agent that can use web search and web scraping to gather data.

params.name: filename
params.description: The filename for the presentation (should end with .pptx).

params.name: title
params.description: The title of the presentation (shown on title slide).

params.name: author
params.description: Optional author name for the presentation metadata.

params.name: theme
params.description: Color theme for the presentation. Options: default, corporate, dark, minimal, creative

params.name: sections
params.description: Section outlines for the presentation. Each section is independently researched and built by a focused sub-agent.

create-text-file.description: Create a text file with arbitrary content. Provide the content and an optional file extension (defaults to .txt). Common extensions include .txt, .md, .json, .csv, .html, .xml, .yaml, .log, etc.

params.name: filename
params.description: The filename for the text file. If no extension is provided, the extension parameter will be used (defaults to .txt).

params.name: extension
params.description: The file extension to use (without the dot). Defaults to 'txt'. Common options: txt, md, json, csv, html, xml, yaml, log, etc.

params.name: content
params.description: The text content to write to the file. Can be any arbitrary text including multi-line content.

create-pdf-file.description: Create a PDF document from markdown or plain text content. The content will be styled and converted to a professional PDF document. Supports markdown formatting including headers, lists, code blocks, tables, and more.

params.name: filename
params.description: The filename for the PDF document. The .pdf extension will be added automatically if not provided.

params.name: content
params.description: The markdown or plain text content to convert to PDF. Supports full markdown syntax including headers (#, ##, ###), bold (**text**), italic (*text*), lists, code blocks, tables, and more.

create-excel-file.description: Create an Excel spreadsheet (.xlsx) from CSV data. Supports multiple sheets, automatic type detection (numbers, dates, booleans), header styling, column auto-fit, zebra striping, and frozen panes. Provide data in CSV format with comma, semicolon, tab, or pipe delimiters.

params.name: filename
params.description: The filename for the Excel file. The .xlsx extension will be added automatically if not provided.

params.name: csvData
params.description: CSV data for a single-sheet workbook. Use comma, semicolon, tab, or pipe as delimiter. For multiple sheets, use the 'sheets' parameter instead.

params.name: sheets
params.description: Array of sheet definitions for multi-sheet workbooks. Each sheet has a name, csvData, and optional styling options.

params.name: options
params.description: Default styling options applied to all sheets (can be overridden per-sheet).

create-docx-file.description: Create a Microsoft Word document (.docx) from markdown or plain text content. Supports professional styling with color themes, title pages, and running headers/footers.

params.name: filename
params.description: The filename for the Word document. Will automatically add .docx extension if not present.

params.name: title
params.description: Document title for metadata and title page. If not provided, will be extracted from content or use filename.

params.name: subtitle
params.description: Optional subtitle displayed on the title page below the main title.

params.name: author
params.description: Optional author name displayed on the title page.

params.name: content
params.description: The content to convert to a Word document. Fully supports markdown formatting.

params.name: theme
params.description: Color theme for the document. 'neutral' (slate/grey), 'blue' (corporate blue), or 'warm' (earthy tones). Defaults to neutral.

params.name: margins
params.description: Page margin preset. 'normal' (standard), 'narrow' (data-heavy docs), or 'wide' (letters/memos). Defaults to normal.

params.name: includeTitlePage
params.description: Include a professional title page with centered title, subtitle, author, and date. Content starts on page 2 with running headers/footers.

gmail-get-inbox.description: Get the inbox emails from Gmail. Returns the inbox emails with the details of the email. Supports optional query and limit parameters to filter the emails.

params.name: query
params.description: Optional Gmail search query. Use Gmail query syntax like 'is:inbox', 'is:unread', 'from:email', 'subject:keyword', etc.

params.name: limit
params.description: Optional maximum number of results to return (1-50). Defaults to 10.

gmail-search.description: Search emails in Gmail using Gmail query syntax. Supports full Gmail search including keywords and operators combined. Common operators: 'is:inbox', 'is:unread', 'is:starred', 'from:email', 'to:email', 'subject:word', 'has:attachment', 'newer_than:7d', 'older_than:1m'. Combine with search terms: 'is:inbox meeting notes' finds inbox emails containing 'meeting notes'. Returns thread summaries with ID, subject, date, and unread status.

params.name: query
params.description: Gmail search query. Use Gmail query syntax like 'is:inbox', 'is:unread', 'from:email', 'subject:keyword', etc.

params.name: limit
params.description: Maximum number of results to return (1-50). Defaults to 10.

params.name: start
params.description: Starting offset for pagination. Defaults to 0.

gmail-read-thread.description: Read a full email thread by its ID. Returns all messages in the thread including sender, recipients, subject, body, date, and attachment information. Use this after searching to read the full conversation.

params.name: threadId
params.description: The Gmail thread ID to read.

gmail-create-draft.description: Create a new draft email in Gmail. The draft will be saved but not sent. You can optionally include CC, BCC recipients, HTML body content, and file attachments.

params.name: to
params.description: Recipient email address(es). Multiple addresses can be comma-separated.

params.name: subject
params.description: Email subject line.

params.name: body
params.description: Plain text email body content.

params.name: cc
params.description: CC recipient email address(es). Optional.

params.name: bcc
params.description: BCC recipient email address(es). Optional.

params.name: htmlBody
params.description: HTML version of the email body. Optional.

params.name: attachments
params.description: Array of absolute file paths to attach to the draft.

gmail-create-draft-reply.description: Create a draft reply to an existing email thread in Gmail. The draft will be saved but not sent. You can choose to reply to all recipients or just the sender. Supports file attachments.

params.name: threadId
params.description: The Gmail thread ID to reply to.

params.name: body
params.description: Plain text reply body content.

params.name: replyAll
params.description: Whether to reply to all recipients. Defaults to false (reply to sender only).

params.name: cc
params.description: Additional CC recipient email address(es). Optional.

params.name: bcc
params.description: BCC recipient email address(es). Optional.

params.name: htmlBody
params.description: HTML version of the reply body. Optional.

params.name: attachments
params.description: Array of absolute file paths to attach to the draft reply.

gmail-update-draft.description: Update an existing draft email in Gmail. You must provide the draft ID and the new content for the draft. Supports file attachments.

params.name: draftId
params.description: The Gmail draft ID to update.

params.name: to
params.description: Recipient email address(es). Multiple addresses can be comma-separated.

params.name: subject
params.description: Email subject line.

params.name: body
params.description: Plain text email body content.

params.name: cc
params.description: CC recipient email address(es). Optional.

params.name: bcc
params.description: BCC recipient email address(es). Optional.

params.name: htmlBody
params.description: HTML version of the email body. Optional.

params.name: attachments
params.description: Array of absolute file paths to attach to the draft.

gmail-get-draft.description: Retrieve a specific draft email by its ID. Returns the draft details including recipient, subject, and body content.

params.name: draftId
params.description: The Gmail draft ID to retrieve.

gmail-list-drafts.description: List all draft emails in Gmail. Returns a summary of each draft including ID, recipient, subject, and date.

params.name: limit
params.description: Maximum number of drafts to return (1-100). Defaults to 25.

gmail-delete-draft.description: Delete a draft email from Gmail. This action is permanent and cannot be undone.

params.name: draftId
params.description: The Gmail draft ID to delete.

gmail-send-draft.description: Send an existing draft email from Gmail. This will send the draft immediately and remove it from drafts. This action cannot be undone.

params.name: draftId
params.description: The Gmail draft ID to send.

gmail-send-email.description: Send an email immediately through Gmail. This action sends the email right away and cannot be undone. For composing emails that need review before sending, use gmail-create-draft instead.

params.name: to
params.description: Recipient email address(es). Multiple addresses can be comma-separated.

params.name: subject
params.description: Email subject line.

params.name: body
params.description: Plain text email body content.

params.name: cc
params.description: CC recipient email address(es). Optional.

params.name: bcc
params.description: BCC recipient email address(es). Optional.

params.name: htmlBody
params.description: HTML version of the email body. Optional.

params.name: replyTo
params.description: Reply-to email address. Optional.

params.name: attachments
params.description: Array of absolute file paths to attach to the email.

gmail-reply-to-thread.description: Reply to an existing email thread immediately. This action sends the reply right away and cannot be undone. For composing replies that need review before sending, use gmail-create-draft-reply instead. Supports file attachments via absolute file paths (max 20MB total for all attachments combined).

params.name: threadId
params.description: The Gmail thread ID to reply to.

params.name: body
params.description: Plain text reply body content.

params.name: replyAll
params.description: Whether to reply to all recipients. Defaults to false (reply to sender only).

params.name: cc
params.description: Additional CC recipient email address(es). Optional.

params.name: bcc
params.description: BCC recipient email address(es). Optional.

params.name: htmlBody
params.description: HTML version of the reply body. Optional.

params.name: attachments
params.description: Array of absolute file paths to attach to the reply.

gmail-mark-read.description: Mark an email thread as read in Gmail. This will mark all messages in the thread as read.

params.name: threadId
params.description: The Gmail thread ID to mark as read.

gmail-mark-unread.description: Mark an email thread as unread in Gmail. This will mark the thread as unread so it appears as a new message.

params.name: threadId
params.description: The Gmail thread ID to mark as unread.

gmail-move-to-trash.description: Move an email thread to trash in Gmail. The thread can be recovered from trash within 30 days.

params.name: threadId
params.description: The Gmail thread ID to move to trash.

gmail-move-to-archive.description: Archive an email thread in Gmail. The thread will be removed from inbox but can still be found in All Mail or by searching.

params.name: threadId
params.description: The Gmail thread ID to archive.

gmail-move-to-inbox.description: Move an email thread back to inbox in Gmail. Use this to unarchive a thread or move it from other locations to inbox.

params.name: threadId
params.description: The Gmail thread ID to move to inbox.

gmail-get-mailbox-stats.description: Used for general account information. Reports Gmail mailbox statistics including unread counts for inbox, priority inbox, starred messages, and spam folder.

outlook-get-inbox.description: Get recent emails from the Outlook inbox. Returns a list of recent messages with subject, sender, date, and read status. Use this to quickly see what's in the inbox.

params.name: limit
params.description: Maximum number of messages to return (1-50). Defaults to 25.

outlook-search.description: Search emails in Outlook using Microsoft Search syntax. Supports searching by keywords, sender, subject, and more. Common search terms: 'from:email', 'subject:word', 'hasAttachments:true'. Returns message summaries with ID, subject, date, and read status.

params.name: query
params.description: Search query. Use Microsoft Search syntax like 'from:email', 'subject:keyword', etc.

params.name: limit
params.description: Maximum number of results to return (1-50). Defaults to 10.

params.name: skip
params.description: Number of results to skip for pagination. Defaults to 0.

outlook-read-thread.description: Read a full email conversation thread by its conversation ID. Returns all messages in the thread including sender, recipients, subject, body, date, and attachment information. Use this after searching to read the full conversation.

params.name: conversationId
params.description: The Outlook conversation ID to read.

outlook-create-draft.description: Create a new draft email in Outlook. The draft will be saved but not sent. Can also create a draft reply to an existing message by providing replyToMessageId. You can optionally include CC, BCC recipients, HTML body content, and file attachments.

params.name: replyToMessageId
params.description: Message ID to reply to. If provided, creates a draft reply instead of a new draft. When replying, 'to' and 'subject' are optional (inherited from original).

params.name: replyAll
params.description: When replying, whether to reply to all recipients. Defaults to false.

params.name: to
params.description: Recipient email address(es). Required for new drafts, optional for replies.

params.name: subject
params.description: Email subject line. Required for new drafts, optional for replies.

params.name: body
params.description: Email body content.

params.name: cc
params.description: CC recipient email address(es). Optional.

params.name: bcc
params.description: BCC recipient email address(es). Optional.

params.name: isHtml
params.description: Whether the body is HTML content. Defaults to false.

params.name: attachments
params.description: Array of absolute file paths to attach to the draft.

outlook-update-draft.description: Update an existing draft email in Outlook. You can modify the recipients, subject, or body of the draft.

params.name: draftId
params.description: The ID of the draft to update.

params.name: to
params.description: New recipient email address(es). Optional.

params.name: subject
params.description: New email subject. Optional.

params.name: body
params.description: New email body content. Optional.

params.name: cc
params.description: New CC recipient email address(es). Optional.

params.name: isHtml
params.description: Whether the body is HTML content. Defaults to false.

outlook-list-drafts.description: List all draft emails in Outlook. Returns a summary of each draft including ID, subject, recipients, and last modified date.

params.name: limit
params.description: Maximum number of drafts to return (1-50). Defaults to 25.

outlook-delete-draft.description: Delete a draft email from Outlook. This permanently removes the draft and cannot be undone.

params.name: draftId
params.description: The ID of the draft to delete.

outlook-send-draft.description: Send an existing draft email from Outlook. This action sends the email immediately and cannot be undone.

params.name: draftId
params.description: The ID of the draft to send.

outlook-send-email.description: Send an email immediately through Outlook. This action sends the email right away and cannot be undone. Can also reply to an existing message by providing replyToMessageId. For composing emails that need review before sending, use outlook-create-draft instead.

params.name: replyToMessageId
params.description: Message ID to reply to. If provided, sends a reply instead of a new email. When replying, 'to' and 'subject' are optional (inherited from original).

params.name: replyAll
params.description: When replying, whether to reply to all recipients. Defaults to false.

params.name: to
params.description: Recipient email address(es). Required for new emails, optional for replies.

params.name: subject
params.description: Email subject line. Required for new emails, optional for replies.

params.name: body
params.description: Email body content.

params.name: cc
params.description: CC recipient email address(es). Optional.

params.name: bcc
params.description: BCC recipient email address(es). Optional.

params.name: isHtml
params.description: Whether the body is HTML content. Defaults to false.

params.name: attachments
params.description: Array of absolute file paths to attach to the email.

outlook-get-mailbox-stats.description: Get Outlook mailbox statistics including folder counts and user profile information. Returns the total and unread counts for inbox, drafts, sent items, and deleted items.

gcal-list-calendars.description: List all Google Calendars the user owns or is subscribed to. Returns calendar names, IDs, time zones, and ownership information. Use this to discover available calendars before querying events.

gcal-get-calendar.description: Get detailed information about a specific Google Calendar by its ID. Returns calendar name, description, time zone, and settings.

params.name: calendarId
params.description: The calendar ID. If omitted, returns the primary calendar.

gcal-get-event.description: Get detailed information about a specific calendar event by its ID. Returns event title, time, location, description, guests, and RSVP status.

params.name: eventId
params.description: The event ID to retrieve.

params.name: calendarId
params.description: Optional calendar ID. If omitted, uses the primary calendar.

gcal-get-events-for-day.description: Get all calendar events for a specific day. Returns event titles, times, and IDs for the specified date.

params.name: date
params.description: The date to query in ISO format (YYYY-MM-DD).

params.name: calendarId
params.description: Optional calendar ID. If omitted, uses the primary calendar.

gcal-get-events.description: Get calendar events within a date range, optionally filtered by search query. Returns event titles, times, and IDs. Use this for custom date ranges.

params.name: startDate
params.description: Start of date range in ISO datetime format.

params.name: endDate
params.description: End of date range in ISO datetime format.

params.name: query
params.description: Optional text to search for in events.

params.name: calendarId
params.description: Optional calendar ID. If omitted, uses the primary calendar.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max results to return (default 25, max 100).

gcal-get-upcoming-events.description: Get upcoming calendar events using simple time period keywords. This is the preferred tool for common queries like 'what's on my calendar today?' Supports periods: 'today', 'tomorrow', 'week' (next 7 days), 'month' (next 30 days), 'next week', and 'next month'. Automatically calculates the correct date range so you don't need to know the current date.

params.name: period
params.type: today | tomorrow | week | this week | next week | month | this month | next month
params.description: Time period to query. Options: 'today', 'tomorrow', 'week' (next 7 days), 'this week', 'next week', 'month' (next 30 days), 'this month', 'next month'.

params.name: query
params.description: Optional text to search for in events.

params.name: calendarId
params.description: Optional calendar ID. If omitted, uses the primary calendar.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max results to return (default 25, max 100).

gcal-quick-add.description: Create a calendar event from a natural language description. Google Calendar will parse the description to extract the event title, date, and time. Examples: 'Meeting with John tomorrow at 3pm', 'Dentist appointment on Friday at 10am'.

params.name: description
params.description: Natural language description of the event including title, date, and time.

params.name: calendarId
params.description: Optional calendar ID. If omitted, uses the primary calendar.

gcal-create-event.description: Create a calendar event with full control over all event properties. Supports timed events, all-day events, and recurring events. For simple events, consider using gcal-quick-add instead.

params.name: title
params.description: The event title.

params.name: startTime
params.description: Start time in ISO datetime format (for timed events).

params.name: endTime
params.description: End time in ISO datetime format (for timed events).

params.name: allDay
params.description: Set to true for all-day events.

params.name: date
params.description: Date in YYYY-MM-DD format (required for all-day events).

params.name: endDate
params.description: End date for multi-day all-day events (YYYY-MM-DD).

params.name: description
params.description: Event description/notes.

params.name: location
params.description: Event location.

params.name: guests
params.description: Array of guest email addresses.

params.name: sendInvites
params.description: Whether to send invite emails to guests.

params.name: calendarId
params.description: Optional calendar ID. If omitted, uses the primary calendar.

params.name: recurrence
params.description: Recurrence configuration for recurring events.

gcal-update-event.description: Update an existing calendar event. You can change the title, description, location, time, or guest list. Only provide the fields you want to update.

params.name: eventId
params.description: The ID of the event to update.

params.name: calendarId
params.description: Optional calendar ID. If omitted, uses the primary calendar.

params.name: title
params.description: New event title.

params.name: description
params.description: New event description.

params.name: location
params.description: New event location.

params.name: startTime
params.description: New start time in ISO datetime format.

params.name: endTime
params.description: New end time in ISO datetime format.

params.name: guests
params.description: New guest list (replaces existing guests). Array of email addresses.

gcal-set-my-status.description: Set your RSVP status for a calendar event. Use this to accept, decline, or tentatively accept meeting invitations.

params.name: eventId
params.description: The ID of the event to RSVP to.

params.name: status
params.description: Your RSVP status: YES (accept), NO (decline), MAYBE (tentative), or INVITED (reset to invited).

params.name: calendarId
params.description: Optional calendar ID. If omitted, uses the primary calendar.

create-scheduled-job.description: Create a recurring Scheduled Job that automatically runs an agent prompt on a schedule (e.g. 'every weekday at 9am summarize my inbox and email me'). Provide `schedule` as a standard 5-field cron expression (minute hour dom month dow) in the USER'S LOCAL TIME - the server automatically converts to UTC. IMPORTANT - the job runs later on its own with NO chat context and can ONLY use the tools you list in `tools`. Tool IDs for scheduled jobs are NOT the same as agent plugin names - you MUST call this tool with `listTools: true` first to get the exact valid IDs, then call it again with your chosen `tools`. Never guess tool IDs - always discover them via `listTools: true` first.

params.name: listTools
params.description: Returns the catalog of valid tool IDs for scheduled jobs. ALWAYS call this first before specifying any `tools` - scheduled job tool IDs are different from agent plugin names and must be discovered, not guessed.

params.name: name
params.description: Short, human-readable name for the scheduled job.

params.name: prompt
params.description: The instruction the agent will execute each time the job runs. Be specific and self-contained - the job runs later with no chat context.

params.name: schedule
params.description: A standard 5-field cron expression in the user's LOCAL time (minute hour dom month dow). The server converts to UTC automatically. Examples: '0 9 * * 1-5' = weekdays at 09:00 local, '30 14 * * *' = daily at 14:30 local, '0 */2 * * *' = every 2 hours (no conversion needed).

params.name: tools
params.description: The tool IDs (from `listTools`) the job is allowed to use when it runs. The job can ONLY use tools listed here, so include every tool the prompt needs to do its work. Omit only if the task genuinely needs no tools - the job will then run with no tools at all.
